# yantra-agent

> The per-machine heartbeat agent. It exists because Tailscale exposes zero telemetry and SSH polling
> cannot see a sleeping laptop, so the scheduler would otherwise be blind to the one question it most
> needs answered. Pushes a heartbeat every 10s; the daemon marks a machine stale at 30s.
> **Implemented apart from its install story.** Deliberately tiny: it reports, it does not decide.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): the 10 s loop, a hand-written HTTP/1.1 POST over
  `std::net::TcpStream`, and the log-once-then-quiet failure latch.
- [src/probes.rs](src/probes.rs): the seven fields, measured. Fixed facts once at start, the rest per beat; every reader fails pessimistic; `Power::Battery` has one construction site.

## What decides its shape

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what it may call, what the loop must keep doing, and its one configuration value.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): the seven fields, the transport, and §7 — drop the beat, never exit, log once.
- [plans/m5-the-heartbeat-agent.md](../../docs/plans/m5-the-heartbeat-agent.md): §1 and §2 measure why there is no HTTP crate and no async runtime; §3 runs every probe on both fleet machines and is the probes' specification; §5 measures the local agent; §8 lists where reality differed from the ADR.
- [yantra-core/src/heartbeat.rs](../yantra-core/src/heartbeat.rs): the wire type, and the only module of the library this binary calls.
- [research/01-tailscale-inventory.md](../../docs/research/01-tailscale-inventory.md): the negative finding that made an agent unavoidable — zero telemetry, verified three ways.
- [research/05-scheduling.md](../../docs/research/05-scheduling.md): why polling over SSH was rejected, and what the scheduler needs from a heartbeat.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): the two invariants that bind this crate. I-9 is a scoring bug in disguise — read it before writing the power-supply reader.
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): R-12 is the risk this crate is the likeliest to realise.
